newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN BRISK TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN BRISK TRADE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were indicated mixed in active trade on Tuesday with most players stocking up on treasury bills in anticipation of a drop in the rates at the next weekly tender, dealers said.
"The market is quite active at the moment. People want to buy treasury bills because we expect rates to fall on the back of increased liquidity," a dealer said.
He said treasury bills were trading at 17.80 percent, slightly down from 17.85 percent the previous day.

NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold at 18.50 and 18.25 percent respectively, unchanged from Monday's levels, while bankers acceptance bills were quoted at 18.25 and 17.85 percent from 18.50 and 17.85 percent.
Call money held steady at 18 percent in a market which was Z$536 million in surplus at settlement.
